source.title: Data Efficiency for Large Recommendation Models
source.authors: Kshitij Jain; Jing-Ru Xie; Kevin Regan; Cheng Chen; Jie Han; Steven Li; Zhuo-Shu Li; Todd Phillips; M. Sussman; M. Troup; Angel Yu; Jian-Heng Zhuo

record.tranche_reason: Tests the compute-allocation idea in a new setting: large recommendation models for ad click prediction.
record.gate_note: The only directly relevant result is the iso-compute experiment in Section 5 / Figure 4. Other data-efficiency and distillation results do not test the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The only scaling-related result is one iso-compute curve for ad-click recommendation models at a single 4K TPU-hour budget, described only as showing 'a clear valley in loss'. One budget cannot show the optimal parameter and token counts growing as a stable power of compute (V3). No power law is fitted in any modality (V5). The subject is not a language model (V1, V2, V4, V6, V7). The result echoes Chinchilla's iso-FLOP shape, but no version's claim is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors present data-efficiency practices for LRMs: pruning after data convergence, continuous downsampling, and continuous distillation (35% less data than later cutover). They also note that jointly tuning data volume and model size at fixed compute reveals an optimal configuration, shown at one 4K TPU-hour budget.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies sampling rate and model size in production recommendation models and measures an iso-compute loss curve; it does not reproduce the language-model experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: For ad-click LRMs at a fixed 4K TPU-hour budget, trading sampling rate against model size gives an iso-compute loss curve with a clear interior minimum, similar to Chinchilla's iso-FLOP curves.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At fixed training compute, loss as a function of the model-size/data split has an interior optimum in large recommendation models.

record.problems: The relevant result is described qualitatively and shown in a figure whose plotted values are unavailable in the supplied text. Only one compute budget is reported, so the study does not establish a trend across budgets.
record.rows_left_out: Sections 2–4 discuss convergence, downsampling, and continuous distillation, but do not report results that test the listed scaling-law versions.

untested.parts: All: no language-model loss power law is fitted.
All: no extrapolation from small runs.
Scaling of the optimal parameter and token counts across compute budgets, and the Kaplan-vs-Hoffmann ratio. Only one budget is reported, in recommendation models.
Whether a power-law form holds for recommendation models. No fit or exponents are reported, only an interior optimum at one budget.

record.verdict_notes: This is a short industry note with no numbers for the iso-compute curve. The introduction's remark that scaling benefits 'have begun to plateau' is anecdotal, with no data behind it. The diminishing returns from more data (data convergence, Fig. 1) are schematic and fit no power law. The reader's 'supports V3' label is removed: an interior optimum at one budget is not evidence that the optimum grows as a stable power of compute.

versions.untested_parts: Whether held-out language-model pretraining loss follows power laws in parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether small-run fits predict much larger language-model runs.

The study tests an optimal size/data configuration at one compute budget, but not whether parameter count and token count follow stable power laws across compute budgets, or whether one grows faster than the other.
Whether architecture details such as depth and width have little effect at fixed parameter count.
Whether the same power-law form holds in other modalities or training regimes.
Whether downstream task performance is predictable from scale or pretraining loss.
Whether fitting choices change exponents or optimal allocations, or scaling curves depart from a single power law.

rows.subject: large recommendation models (ad click models)
rows.operation_detail: Varied sampling rate and model size at fixed training compute to plot an iso-compute curve.
rows.measure: Loss / quality along the iso-compute curve
rows.value: figure only; text reports a clear valley in loss and an optimal model-size and sampling-rate configuration
rows.note: The text describes a clear loss valley for the stated 4K TPU-hour budget, but the plotted values are not present in the supplied text. This supports an optimum at that budget, not a stable power-law trend across budgets.
rows.check: A single-budget iso-compute valley in ad-click LRMs cannot show V3's claim that the optimal size and data grow as a stable power of compute. It also fits no power law, so it does not bear on V5. The values are figure-only: no axis numbers, model sizes or sampling rates appear in the text. The subject is recommendation models, not language models.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: LRM ad click models at a fixed budget of 4K TPU hours
reader_labels.reason: The reported iso-compute curve has a clear loss valley, indicating an optimal model-size and sampling-rate configuration at this budget (r1).
